text:
oliver: Hey team — quick help needed. My domestic partner had an ER visit in Barcelona last week and I paid €220. We had a civil partnership ceremony in Spain but haven't registered anything here. Can I add them retroactively and file a reimbursement? What docs will carriers accept for a domestic partner from abroad?

marta (Benefits): Hi Oliver — short answer: possibly. Carriers vary on what they accept as proof of eligible partner status. For retro enrollment + claim we typically ask for: 1) Dependent Enrollment Form signed; 2) Civil partnership certificate (official Spanish registro) OR marriage certificate; 3) Proof of shared residence or financial interdependence (joint lease, joint bank statement, utility in both names) — if none, some carriers accept a notarized domestic partner affidavit; 4) Partner passport ID page; 5) Itemized ER invoice + payment proof; 6) English translation of non-English docs (certified translation preferred); 7) Currency conversion evidence (bank statement or official FX rate). Email all to benefits@redwood.com with subject: "Retro Partner Add - Oliver".

oliver: Thanks. The clinic gave a stamp receipt in Catalan and a short handwritten note. Is that enough?

sophie: Handwritten docs can slow things. Ask the clinic for an itemized bill with CPT-like codes if available and a clinic stamp. If they can't, include a scanned photo of the clinic sign + contact info so carrier can try to reach the provider.

benefits-bot: Automated: Dependent Enrollment Form -> https://intranet.redwood.com/forms/dependent-enroll. Typical carrier adjudication for retro adds: 4-8 weeks. Internal intake confirmation within 1-2 business days. For urgent medical bills, include "URGENT: Retro Med" in subject to request expedited review.

marta (Benefits): Also note: some carriers require domestic partnerships to be registered in the policyholder's home country or provide proof of a qualifying relationship per their policy. We'll check carrier-specific rules after you submit docs and advise whether a notarized affidavit will suffice.

oliver: If carrier denies direct billing, do I file for reimbursement only after the partner is added? I want to avoid double payment.

marta (Benefits): We can submit a retro enrollment request and concurrently request claims reprocessing, but carriers generally need the dependent on file before paying. We will flag the claim as tied to the retro request. If enrollment is approved with an effective date before the service, reimbursement may be allowed. Not guaranteed.

oliver: Understood. Any tips for the translation? I can use an online translator but don't know if that's acceptable.

sophie: Use a certified translator if possible. If not, get a brief notarized translation statement from a local translator or embassy service. Put original + translation together to avoid back-and-forth.

marta (Benefits): Once you send the email we can also generate an internal benefits confirmation letter (1 business day) you can present to the hospital for any upcoming follow-ups. That helps if they ask for insurer proof.

oliver: Great — I'll gather the civil record, passport scan, clinic invoice + translation and send tonight. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

benefits-bot: Reminder: attach PDF copies, not photos if possible. For photos use high-res scans.
